_meanings: A woman of oneʼs own caste.
a follower of the Nyāya system of philosophy.

oneʼs own duty or sway; {#svADikArAt pramattaH#} <ls>Me. 1</ls>;
 {#svADikAraBUmO#} <ls>Ś. 7</ls>.
one of the six Chakras or mystical circles of the body.

.²1 dependent on oneself, self-dependent.
.²2 independent.
.²3 oneʼs own subject.
.²4 in oneʼs own power; {#svADInA vavanIyatApi hi varaM badDo na sevAYjaliH#}
 <ls>Mk. 3. 11</ls>.

{%a.%} having prosperity in oneʼs own power; {#svADInakuSalAH#}
 {#sidDimantaH#} <ls>Ś. 4</ls>.

.²1 self-recitation, muttering to oneself.
.²2 study of the Vedas, sacred study, perusal of sacred books; {#svADyAyenArcayedfzIn#}
 <ls>Ms. 3. 81</ls>; <ls>Bg. 16. 1</ls>; <ls>T. Up. 1. 9. 1</ls>.
.²3 the Veda itself.
.²4 a day on which sacred study is enjoined to be resumed after suspension.

{%m.%} a student who tries to secure his own livelihood during
 his course of holy study; <ls>Ms. 11. 1</ls>.

.²1 a student of the Vedas.
.²2 a tradesman.

.²1 the mind; {#mama svAntaDvAntaM tirayatu navIno jalaDaraH#} <ls>Bv. 4. 5</ls>; <ls>Mv. 7. 17</ls>.
.²2 a cavern.
.²3 oneʼs own death, end.

.²1 self-interested.
.²2 having its own or true meaning.
.²3 having oneʼs own object or aim.
.²4 pleonastic.
.

inference for
 oneself, a kind of inductive reasoning, one of the two main kinds of {#anumAna#},
 the other being {#parArTAnumAna#}.

subject to, or dependent upon, oneself; {#svAyattamekAntaguRaM#}
 {#viDAtrA vinirmitaM CAdanamajYatAyAH#} <ls>Bh. 2. 7</ls>.
the rising of a sign or heavenly body at any particular place.

oneʼs own duty ({#svaDarma#}); {#svakarmanirataH sidDiM#}
 {#yaTA vindati tacCfRu#} <ls>Bg. 18. 45</ls>.

minding oneʼs own duty; {#aDIyIraMstrayo varRAH#}
 {#svakarmasTA dvijAtayaH#} <ls>Ms. 10. 1</ls>.
a deed done by oneʼs self.

experiencing the results of former deeds ({#prArabDakarma#});
 {#mA SocataM mahABAgAvAtmajAn svakftaMBujaH#} <ls>Bhāg. 10. 4. 18</ls>.
subject to oneʼs self; {#svagocare satyapi cittahAriRA#} <ls>Ki. 8. 13</ls>.

oneʼs own will or choice, own fancy or pleasure, independence.
.

{%ind.%} at oneʼs own will or pleasure, wantonly, voluntarily;
 {#svacCandaM daladaravinda te marandaM vindanto vidaDatu guYjitaM milindAH#} <ls>Bv. 1. 15</ls>.
.²2 oneʼs own people or kindred, oneʼs household.

{%a.%} distantly
 related to. ({#svajanAyate#} <ab>Den.</ab> <ab>P.</ab> ‘becomes or is treated as a relation’; <ls>Pt. 1. 5.</ls>)

.²1 oneʼs own kind.
.²2 oneʼs own family or caste.
personal regard or interest; {#asyAM me mahatI svatA#} <ls>Svapna. 1. 7</ls>.

seeing oneʼs self; {#Iyate BagavAneBiH saguRo nirguRaH#}
 {#svadfk#} <ls>Bhāg. 3. 32. 36</ls>.

.²1 oneʼs own religion.
.²2 oneʼs own duty, the duties of oneʼs own class; <ls>Ms. 1. 88</ls>, <ls n="Ms. 1.">91</ls>; {#svaDarme#}
 {#niDanaM SreyaH paraDarmo BayAvahaH#} <ls>Bg. 3. 35</ls>.
.²3 peculiarity, oneʼs own rights.

depending on or subservient to oneself; ({#purARi#}
 {#ca#}) {#nigfhya nigrahABijYo ninye netA svaniGnatAm#} <ls>Śiva B. 25. 9</ls>.

.²1 oneʼs own side or party.
.²2 a friend.
.²3 oneʼs own opinion.
oneʼs own and an enemyʼs country.
by means of oneʼs own efforts.

the doctrine that the universe was produced and is sustained by the natural
 and necessary action of substances according to their inherent properities,
 (and not by the agency of a Supreme Being).

.²1 an epithet of Brahman.
.²2 of Śiva.
.²3 of Viṣṇu. --{%f.%} oneʼs own country, home.
the line which joins the extremities of the perpendicular and diagonal.

.²1 natural taste.
.²2 proper taste or sentiment in composition.
.²3 a kind of astringent juice.
.²4 the residue of oily substances (ground on a stone.)

.²1 independent dominion or sovereignty.
.²2 own kingdom.

.²1 similar, like.
.²2 handsome, pleasing, lovely.
.²3 learned, wise.
.

.²1 oneʼs own form or shape, natural state or condition; {#tatrAnyasya#}
 {#kaTaM na BAvi jagato yasmAt svarUpaM hi tat#} <ls>Pt. 1. 159</ls>.
.²2 natural character or form, true constitution.
.²3 nature.
.²4 peculiar aim.
.²5 kind, sort, species.

{%f.%} one of the three forms of fallacy
 called {#asidDa#} <ab>q. v.</ab>
possessed of property; {#svavatI SrutyanuroDAt#} <ls>ŚB. on MS. 6. 1. 20</ls>.

a woman whether married or unmarried who continues to
 live after maturity in her fatherʼs house.
the knowledge of oneʼs own or the true essence.

.²1 self-abiding.
.²2 self-possession.
.²3 absorption in oneʼs own self; {#unmattamattajaqavatsvasaMsTAM gatasya#}
 {#me vIra cikitsitena#} <ls>Bhāg. 5. 10. 13</ls>.

.²1 self-abiding.
.²2 self-dependent, relying on oneʼs own exertions, confident, firm, resolute;
 {#svasTaM taM sUcayantIva vaYcito'sIti vIkzitEH#} <ls>Bu. Ch. 4. 37</ls>.
.²3 independent.
.²4 doing well, well, in health, at ease, comfortable; {#svasTa evAsmi#}
 <ls>Māl. 4</ls>; {#svasTe ko vA na paRqitaH#} <ls>Pt. 1. 127</ls>; see {#asvasTa#} also.
.²5 contented, happy.
.

oneʼs own place or home, oneʼs own abode; {#nakraH svasTAnamAsAdya#}
 {#gajendramapi karzati#} <ls>Pt. 3. 46</ls>.
oneʼs own hand or handwriting, an autograph; see under {#hasta#}.
oneʼs own good or advantage, oneʼs own welfare.
